title: 09. Evaluation: Evaluation, tracing & monitoring — learning path
summary: Audience: You already know LLMs, RAG, agents, agentic AI basics.
objectives: The Three Layers of AI Quality

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
> **Audience**: You already know LLMs, RAG, agents, agentic AI basics. This guide fills the gap: **how do we measure, trace, monitor, and trust these systems in production?**
>
> **Reading time**: ~4–6 hours total across 12 files.
> **Level**: Intermediate (concept + code + metrics + interview prep).

sections.title: Why This Guide Exists
sections.body:
You can *build* an agent or RAG pipeline. But can you answer:

- "Is my RAG actually retrieving the right context?"
- "Is my agent picking the right tool 90% of the time or 40%?"
- "Why did the model produce this hallucinated answer at 3 AM?"
- "Has my user-feedback score dropped 15% this week — why?"
- "What's a 'golden dataset' and why do I need one before shipping?"

If you can't answer those, you can't ship to production. **Evaluation, tracing, and monitoring are the difference between a demo and a product.**

sections.title: Core Vocabulary (Memorize These)
sections.body:
| Term | One-Line Definition |
|------|---------------------|
| **Evaluation** | Systematic measurement of model/system quality against a defined criterion |
| **Metric** | A specific numeric measurement (e.g., faithfulness = 0.87) |
| **Benchmark** | A standardized dataset + scoring procedure for comparison (MMLU, HumanEval) |
| **Golden dataset** | Curated, labeled examples that serve as ground truth for evaluation |
| **Tracing** | Recording the full execution path of a request (every LLM call, tool call, retrieval) |
| **Span** | A single unit of work in a trace (one LLM call, one tool call, one retrieval) |
| **Trace** | A collection of spans forming one full request's journey |
| **Monitoring** | Continuous observation of a production system's behavior over time |
| **Drift** | Statistical change in inputs or outputs over time (data/concept/prediction drift) |
| **LLM-as-judge** | Using a strong LLM (e.g., GPT-4) to evaluate outputs of another model |
| **Hallucination** | Model output that is fluent but factually wrong or unsupported |
| **Faithfulness** | Does the answer rely only on retrieved context? (no fabrication) |

sections.title: The Three Layers of AI Quality
sections.body:
```mermaid graph TD A[AI SYSTEM QUALITY] --> B[Layer 1: Component Eval] A --> C[Layer 2: System Eval] A --> D[Layer 3: Production Observability] B --> B1[LLM quality
BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-judge] B --> B2[Retriever quality
Recall@k/NDCG] B --> B3[Tool-use quality
selection accuracy] C --> C1[End-to-end task success] C --> C2[User satisfaction] C --> C3[Cost/latency tradeoff] D --> D1[Tracing] D --> D2[Drift detection] D --> D3[Alerting & feedback] ```

sections.title: Mental Model: "The Eval Pyramid"
sections.body:
```
                  ▲
                 ╱ ╲
                ╱   ╲           ← PRODUCTION MONITORING
               ╱─────╲             (live users, drift, alerts)
              ╱       ╲
             ╱  ONLINE ╲         ← TRACING + OBSERVABILITY
            ╱  EVAL    ╲           (sample real traffic, score it)
           ╱────────────╲
          ╱              ╲       ← OFFLINE EVALUATION
         ╱   GOLDEN SET   ╲        (curated test cases, metrics)
        ╱   + BENCHMARKS   ╲
       ╱────────────────────╲   ← UNIT TESTS
      ╱   ASSERTIONS / RULES ╲     (regex, JSON schema, toxicity)
     ╱________________________╲
```

**Read bottom-up**: You can't have reliable online eval without offline eval. You can't have reliable monitoring without tracing. Each layer supports the one above.

sections.title: Next Step
sections.body:
Open **`01-llm-evaluation.md`** to start with foundational LLM evaluation. That file lays the vocabulary and mental models that every later file assumes.

> **Tip**: Keep a notebook open while reading. When you see a metric, write down: *"When would I use this? When would I NOT use this?"* That habit will make you dangerous in interviews.
